subject: Latency fitment checklist & demo availability — Everwell
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@everwell.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Latency fitment checklist & demo availability — Everwell

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the set of asks so we can scope a short hosted demo + bench (goal: p95/p99 fitment for your production traffic, compare hosted Redwood vs your incumbent). I tried to keep this tight so engineering can turn around a test plan quickly.

Key targets we heard from you on the call:
- Desired end-to-end p95: <= 350 ms
- Desired end-to-end p99: <= 900 ms
- Typical request size: ~120 tokens (avg), up to 512 tokens (max)
- Streaming: partial response streaming required; client expects first token within ~150–200 ms for common queries
- Throughput envelope: baseline 30 qps sustained; peak bursts up to 50 concurrent requests; burst duration typically 2–5 minutes

What we (Redwood) will validate in the hosted bench:
- Single-turn latency (cold and warm KV-cache conditions) at 30 qps sustained
- Burst behavior: 50 concurrent sustained for 3 mins to observe tail behavior and degradation modes
- Streaming latency: time-to-first-byte and per-chunk latency (32-token chunking)
- p95/p99 computed end-to-end from request initiation to final token received by client (we'll instrument both server and client capture)

Immediate asks for you to enable a clean bench:
1) Share a small traffic trace or sample payloads (100–200 requests) — helps pick model variant and tokenization assumptions.
2) Confirm whether system prompts or external tool-calls are used in 10%+ of requests (affects decoder behavior).
3) Provide preferred demo/bench windows next week (we're tentatively holding Sep 14–16).

Attachments: I attached a short SLO fitment checklist (slo_fitment_checklist_v1.xlsx) and a sample schema for streaming payloads.

Proposed success criteria for this POC run:
- Hosted Redwood meets desired p95 target for the baseline traffic profile; and
- p99 is below your acceptable ceiling with clear mitigation options (concurrency sharding, prefix caching, and fallback model) documented in the bench report.

Next steps: once you share the sample payloads we'll produce a 48-hour test plan and propose one 3-hour slot for the live demo + 6-hour controlled benchmark run.

Thanks — I'll loop Alex on the engineering details once we have the traces.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: Samira Khan <samira@everwell.ai>

Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency fitment checklist & demo availability — Everwell

Thanks Lauren — this is perfect, appreciate the crisp summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- The p95/p99 targets you listed match our internal goals (<=350ms p95, <=900ms p99).
- Our incumbent typically reports ~420ms p95 and ~1.2s p99 for the 120-token median workload today — so we'd like to see clear improvement.
- Streaming: yes, we stream partial results for most chat flows. Time-to-first-byte is critical for perceived latency.
- Concurrency: peaks can hit ~50 concurrent client connections; we use short-lived spikes during onboarding flows.

I'll push a redacted sample payload set (100 requests) and a 24-hour trace extract to the Drive link you provided. Can you confirm whether you'll run the bench from your hosted environment (public API) or via a dedicated sandbox in our VPC?

For scheduling Sep 14–16 works for our team; prefer 9–12 PDT on the 15th if you can.

Attaching a small file with tokenization notes (sample_streaming_payloads.jsonl).

Regards,
Samira Khan
Sr. Product Manager, AI
Everwell Solutions
samira@everwell.ai

From: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@everwell.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency fitment checklist & demo availability — Everwell

Looping in some engineering detail so Samira knows what we'll need for a representative bench. Quick questions / assumptions below — please confirm: 

Assumptions we plan to validate:
- Model family: we'll start with a 13B quantized variant (Redwood-13B-q4) unless tokenization/sketch suggests otherwise.
- Chunking: streaming 32-token chunks for the initial run.
- KV-cache warm vs cold: we'll run cold-first-request and warm (after 50 requests).
- Network: p95/p99 will be measured end-to-end. For the hosted run we'll report both server-side and client-observed latencies so you can see network delta.

Questions:
1) Can you confirm average payload byte size (we only have token counts)? sample_streaming_payloads.jsonl helps but a quick note on average request bytes is useful.
2) Any TLS termination or edge caching on your side we should be aware of? If you have a proxy that adds 20–60 ms typical latency that will affect p95; we can exclude it from “server-only” metrics but will include it for end-to-end.
3) Do you require the bench to simulate user typing behavior (slow-input streaming) or only server push streaming?

Proposed bench parameters (tentative):
- Baseline: 30 qps sustained for 30 minutes (12k requests)
- Burst: 50 concurrent for 3-minute bursts repeated 3x with 5-minute recovery windows
- Streaming: record time-to-first-byte and inter-chunk latencies for 32-token chunks

If Samira can confirm (1) avg request bytes, (2) whether to include your edge latency as part of the SLA, and (3) confirm sample payloads, we can lock the test plan and calendar invite for Sep 15 9–12 PDT.

— Alex
Senior Engineer, Performance
Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@everwell.ai>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency fitment checklist & demo availability — Everwell

Alex — answers inline:

1) Avg request bytes: ~1.6–2.4 KB (text prompts + metadata); max observed ~9 KB during heavy metadata-enriched flows.
2) TLS/edge: we do terminate TLS at our edge (FastEdge CDN) — typical added latency ~25–35 ms; include this in the end-to-end numbers. For the server-only comparison you can report delta as you suggested.
3) Typing behavior: not required for the bench; server push streaming is sufficient.

I've uploaded the 100-request sample payload file and a small trace extract to the Drive folder you shared. Confirmed: Sep 15 9–12 PDT works for us.

Thanks — see you then.

— Samira
